$comment: Parameters passed to a data-pack generator. A pack whose body declares <sequence name="domain"> accepts domain="…" from the caller, and the engine replaces that sequence with the constant. This was a reference-only feature: the four ports had no notion of it and refused the whole config with TDC015, so the same .tdc file ran in one implementation and failed in four. Nothing here caught it, which is why these cases exist.

cases.name: declared-parameter-is-accepted
cases.description: `domain` is a local <sequence> of common.internet.email, so the caller may set it
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="E"><gen type="template" value="common.internet.email" domain="example.test"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{E}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: undeclared-parameter-is-refused
cases.description: A name the pack does not declare would be silently ignored, which is what makes a typo dangerous
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="E"><gen type="template" value="common.internet.email" nosuch="x"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{E}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-plain-list-pack-takes-no-parameters
cases.description: person.lastName is a list of values — it has no parameters at all, so the attribute does nothing
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="template" value="person.lastName" domain="x"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>
